findings.issue: PostgreSQL 19 adds two brand-new progress-reporting views that the spec does not mention anywhere — not in scope, not in the anti-rework boundary, not in the deferred list: `pg_stat_progress_repack` and `pg_stat_progress_data_checksums` (PG 19 progress-reporting docs list 8 sections vs 6 in PG 18). PG 19 also adds the `REPACK` command, which 'replaces VACUUM FULL and CLUSTER' (release notes), plus `REPACK ... CONCURRENTLY`. `pg_stat_progress_cluster` survives explicitly as a backwards-compatibility view that 'will translate any REPACK command into one of these other two', and it keeps every column pgcenter selects (`cluster_index_relid`, `heap_tuples_scanned`, `heap_tuples_written`, `heap_blks_*`) — so nothing breaks. But the spec's enumeration of the PG 19 progress surface is presented as complete (three new columns on three screens, everything else routed to [016]-[018]), and these two views fall outside that map entirely.
findings.why_matters: Two consequences. (1) Product: on PG 19 a DBA running `REPACK` sees it on pgcenter's `progress_cluster` screen under a translated `CLUSTER`/`VACUUM FULL` identity, and the repack-specific data — `heap_tuples_inserted`/`updated`/`deleted`, `repack_index_relid`, the CONCURRENTLY phases — is simply not reachable from pgcenter. That is exactly the 'pgcenter tracks current PostgreSQL statistics' promise this feature exists to keep, and REPACK is the headline table-rewrite command of PG 19. (2) Planning: because neither the spec nor `docs/roadmap-0.12.0.md` names these views, no later feature owns them — unlike the WAL/slots/tables columns, which have explicit owners. A gap with no owner is discovered after the release, not before it.
findings.fix: Add one bullet to «Ограничения» naming both views with an explicit disposition — e.g. 'PG 19 adds `pg_stat_progress_repack` and `pg_stat_progress_data_checksums`; new screens for them are out of scope for 0.12.0 and are registered as a 0.13.0 candidate. `REPACK` remains visible on the existing `progress_cluster` screen via the backwards-compatibility view.' Add the corresponding check to the verification pass (step 5 / AC 3): run a `REPACK` on the PG 19 cluster and confirm the `progress_cluster` screen renders the row and that every column pgcenter selects is still populated from the compat view.

findings.issue: Implementation detail still sits in the user-spec, though less of it than in round 1. The uniform-selector-arity decision is gone (confirmed), but three items remain: the constant name plus its file — «Константа `PostgresV19 = 190000` в `internal/query/query.go`» (line 16); the code shape of the version selectors — «все версионные селекторы написаны через неравенства (`version >= PostgresV18`)» (line 28); and the query-internals justification for the blank-cell UX — «Экран вакуума собирает строки через `RIGHT JOIN` к `pg_stat_activity`» (line 116).
findings.why_matters: User-spec answers WHAT and WHY; a reader has to hold the `internal/query` package layout in their head to follow these three sentences, and a file path in an approved user-spec reads as a commitment the tech-spec must honour rather than a fact it should re-derive. This is now cosmetic rather than structural — none of the three freezes a decision the way the arity choice did, and the `>=` fact is genuinely load-bearing evidence for the 'nothing breaks by construction' argument — so it is cheap to fix and does not block approval.
findings.fix: Reword in place, keep the argument: 'pgcenter learns to recognise server version 190000' (drop the constant name and file); 'all version selectors are written as `newest branch if version is at or above the latest known version`, so a new major lands in the newest branch by construction' (keep the fact, drop the identifier); 'a vacuum row can appear on the screen before a progress record exists for it — those cells render blank' (drop the RIGHT JOIN). Move the exact names/paths into the tech-spec, where the code research already has them (§1.1, §7.6).

findings.issue: The reconciled AC 3 / risk 5 escape hatch has no fallback branch. A breakage found on PG 19 in a re-entered area is fixed by [016]/[017]/[018], recorded by name with its owning feature, and re-verified at release finalization — the guarantee 'на момент выпуска ни один экран не остаётся сломанным' rests entirely on those features shipping inside 0.12.0. Nothing in the spec says what happens if one of them is dropped, deferred to 0.13.0, or descoped — the deferred fix then has no owner and the guarantee fails silently.
findings.why_matters: This is the residual half of the round-1 AC 3 finding. The reconciliation is sound as long as the release holds together; the failure mode is a planning event (a feature slips), which is exactly the kind of thing that happens after [012] is closed and archived, when nobody re-reads its acceptance criteria. The release-finalization re-check would catch it, but only if someone knows to look for a list that lives in a closed feature's report.
findings.fix: One clause on the risk-5 mitigation: 'if the owning feature is dropped from 0.12.0, the fix returns to this feature's scope (or blocks the 0.12.0 release) — a deferred PG 19 breakage never leaves 0.12.0 unfixed.' Also state where the named list lives so finalization can find it (the feature's Post-implementation section).

findings.issue: The `pgdg-testing` guard is a remembered manual step, and its stated rationale does not match how the Dockerfile installs packages. The spec says leaving the repo line in place means 'следующая пересборка образа молча затянет бету PG 20 в слот PG 19'. `testing/Dockerfile` names every package explicitly (`postgresql-14 ... postgresql-18`), so a leftover `jammy-pgdg-testing` line cannot substitute PG 20 for PG 19. What it actually does is (a) keep PG 19 itself on the beta/RC channel across rebuilds after GA — including the GA-verification rebuild the spec relies on — and (b) silently hand a beta build to whoever adds `postgresql-20` in a future release.
findings.why_matters: Consequence (a) is the one that bites this release: the RC/GA re-verification pass is the spec's declared remedy for beta drift, and if the repo line is still there the rebuild may re-install a testing-channel PG 19 and re-verify against the same beta family it was trying to move off. The spec accepted precisely this reasoning one section earlier — it chose to fix the `NewTestConnectVersion` fallback structurally rather than defend it with a ritual — and the same reasoning applies here.
findings.fix: Correct the rationale ('the testing repo keeps PG 19 on the beta channel across rebuilds, and hands a beta build to the next version added') and prefer a structural guard over a remembered step: apt pinning (`Pin: release n=jammy-pgdg-testing` restricted to `postgresql-19*` with an explicit priority) or a pinned package version, so the beta channel cannot leak to any other package and the GA rebuild cannot silently re-install a beta. Keep the deferred removal item either way.

summary: Round 1's critical is genuinely closed — independently verified against the PG 19 docs: the release notes contain no removed columns in the stats views, the single stats rename is `pg_stat_subscription_stats.sync_error_count` → `sync_table_error_count` (pgcenter does not query that view — zero grep hits), the `BUFFERPIN` → `BUFFER` type rename touches nothing (the only hardcoded wait-event literals are `'Lock'`), and all three new columns exist in PG 19 with exactly the values the spec lists; the three majors and three minors are addressed too. Approved, with one substantive gap left: PG 19's two brand-new progress views (`pg_stat_progress_repack`, `pg_stat_progress_data_checksums`) and the new `REPACK` command are absent from the spec's otherwise complete PG 19 map, so they have no owner in the release — plus residual implementation detail and two small hardening nits.
